# NEUTROPENIC ENTEROCOLITIS (TYPHLITIS)

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

Neutropenic enterocolitis, also known as "typhlitis" or "necrotizing enterocolitis", is a severe intraabdominal infection that occurs in neutropenic patients, especially in those with acute leukemia. Send stool for C. difficile testing to exclude of C. difficile infection.
[Clostridioides difficile infection](clostridiodes-difficile-infection)

Hematology-oncology, Infectious Diseases and general surgery consults are essential. Broad spectrum antimicrobials that include anaerobic coverage should be initiated promptly.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Continue antimicrobial therapy until normalization of body temperature, recovery of neutropenia (unless planning to transition back to antimicrobial prophylaxis), recovery of thrombocytopenia, return of normal gastrointestinal function and resolution of bacteremia if initially present. Infectious Disease consult recommended to guide duration if perforation, abscess, or other complicating feature present.

References:
Mandell chapter: Diverticulitis and typhlitis
NCCN Prevention & treatment of cancer-related infections Version 1.2024
Nesher and Rolston, Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2013, 56(5):711-7
Sanford Guide article: Neutropenic Enterocolitis, Typhlitis
Up-to-Date article: Neutropenic enterocolitis (typhlitis)
Freifeld AG Clin Infect Dis 2011, 52: e56
Therapy:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]
< OR >
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

## Alternative

Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
